newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CBA launches new securitisation programme.
newsitem.headline: CBA launches new securitisation programme.

text.p: The Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) has launched a programme to securitise loan assets from motor vehicle fleet programmes, the bank said on Thursday.
CBA said it was the first major bank securitisation of non-housing loan assets and the first securitisation by the CBA of its own assets.
"The securitisation launched today comprises the Bank's A$178 million loan in respect of the South Australian government vehicle fleet transaction," CBA said.
"The bank has ultimately sold the loan to GLASS (Generic Loan Asset Securitisation Structure) which will issue S&P rated A-1 plus commercial paper to fund the purchase," it said.
GLASS is a generic securitisation vehicle developed by CBA's Corporate Finance and Financial Markets teams.
CBA later said it aimed to securitise about A$500 million to A$600 million worth of government car fleet lease assets over the next two to three months.

CBA said it had completed the purchase of the New South Wales government vehicle fleet for A$150 million and would complete shortly a A$200 million purchase of the Victorian government's fleet on top of the A$200 million South Australian fleet purchase.
CBA Vice President of Corporate Finance Jim Eldridge said CBA aimed to securitise these A$550 million worth of assets.

"The Victorian asset is a very similar type of asset and we'd look at a very similar type of transaction there, and the intention would be to use the vehicle to securitise that (the New South Wales fleet) as well," he said.
CBA said the securitisation of these assets would have the effect of diversifying risk and reducing overall capital requirements.

"This securitisation programme rounds off our expertise and dominant position in the large motor vehicle fleet lease market and is very positive for our profile in other structured finance business," CBA's Head of Corporate Finance Irene Lee said in a

CBA said future opportunities for buying government car fleets included the A$300 million Queensland government car fleet, a further A$200 million New South Wales government programme and the potential A$400 million programme from the Federal government through the DAS (Department of Administrative Services) Fleet.
CBA Head of Financial Markets Distribution Neil Schafer said there was a strong appetite for non-mortgage securitised assets because of pricing and diversification benefits.
"Originators are also attracted because of the margins and the shortage of tradeable fixed interest securities in the Australian market," Schafer said in a statement.
CBA said it intended to use GLASS to securitise government and fleet lease assets owned by CBA, as well as other asset classes.
